scope: Evaluate whether S-P-O-compatible recovered language-use evidence should remain local or justify broader word-order design testing.

evidence.observation: AN precedes ZAMI and ZAMO follows ZAMI. Under B14 AN is a scoped first-person referent. This is compatible with a PERSON-REFERENT -> LANGUAGE-USE-PREDICATE -> CONTENT linear frame.
Repeats AN -> ZAMI -> specific language-name linear order, but exact sentence meaning is unrecovered. It supports distributional repetition, not an independent semantic proof.
EN precedes ZAMI, content follows ZAMI, and KE is clause-final. B14 and B15 independently govern only the scoped EN and KE roles.
Shares EN -> ZAMI -> content-phrase -> KE ordering but cannot be given a new exact gloss.

evidence.observation: Has a substantially different internal sequence and blocks any claim that all recovered clauses instantiate one simple SVO template.

analysis.strongest_supported_generalization: A narrow language-use frame is compatible with [PERSON_REFERENT] [ZAMI] [LANGUAGE_CONTENT], with KE following the frame in governed question-like use.

analysis.authority_boundary: Compatibility in one recovered microdomain is stronger than pure speculation but weaker than a general basic-word-order rule.

options.effect: Recognize the [PERSON_REFERENT] [ZAMI] [LANGUAGE_CONTENT] linear frame as governed and scoped to recovered/approved language-use constructions. Treat S-P-O as an analytical compatibility label only, not a universal grammar rule. Broader word-order design remains unresolved.

options.risk: Would move from local evidence to cross-domain design before other predicate classes, possession, modality and clause types are governed.
